entries.title: A phone-first shell
entries.body: On a phone the app now has its own chrome: the top bar slides away as you scroll and returns the moment you scroll up, taking the multi-profile "Viewing N profiles" banner with it so you always know whose data you're reading. The bar carries one-tap Search and a contextual + button that starts the current page's obvious log — food on Nutrition, a dose on Medications, weight on Body — with a quick-log sheet behind it for everything else. The drawer learns your most-visited pages as Frequent shortcuts (kept on your device only), spacing tightens below tablet width, and every animation honors your system's reduced-motion setting.

entries.title: Offline dose logs are timed right and never lie
entries.body: A dose you confirm without signal is now logged at the moment you tapped it — not when your phone reconnected — so adherence history reflects when you actually took it. Replays also go through the exact same checks as a normal tap: a medication you paused, a dose the day already resolved, or an entry that sat queued too long is parked in the review panel with a plain-language reason instead of being reported as synced. This also fixes a real bug where a queued confirm could log a dose — and burn supply — for a paused medication.

entries.title: Share one bottle across the household
entries.body: A medication or supplement can now link to a shared bottle in the new household cabinet. Everyone's doses draw from the same count — each person at their own dose size — days-remaining reflects the whole household's pace, and a low bottle raises exactly one alert, never one per person. Items you don't share keep their private counts.

entries.title: Release notes, right here in the app
entries.body: This page is new. It ships with the app itself, so after an update you can see what changed without leaving Allos — even offline. The small dot on the What's new link marks notes you haven't read yet and clears when you visit.

entries.title: Steadier phone-at-the-gym flow
entries.body: During a live workout the screen now stays awake only while the workout is actually in front of you — minimizing it to the dock releases the screen again (previously the phone could stay awake indefinitely). The rest timer's finish and each set check-off also give a short vibration cue on phones that support it, skipped when reduced motion is on.

entries.title: A day at a glance on the Timeline
entries.body: Opening a single day on the Timeline now shows the day on a clock: your heart-rate curve, sleep and workout blocks, and small tick marks for the day's timed events. Tapping a tick jumps to that entry in the list below. The panel appears only when the day has that kind of data.

entries.title: Merge duplicate workouts in one step
entries.body: The same workout arriving from more than one source can now be merged as a whole group — the cluster card on Data → Review, or several entries selected together in the Journal. After a sync, near-certain duplicates are merged for you; every automatic merge is listed so you can look at what it did and undo it.

entries.title: Symptoms and photos gather onto the illness episode
entries.body: A symptom logged while an illness episode is open now attaches to that episode by itself, and a photo can be tagged to the specific symptom entry it shows. The episode page pulls it all together, so a sick week reads as one story instead of scattered entries.

entries.title: Faster family access editor
entries.body: The login-by-profile access grid now opens as one compact summary row per login, and the grant controls load only when you start editing that row. A household with many logins and profiles reaches the screen far quicker.

entries.title: Health Connect token stored hashed, plus per-sync record details
entries.body: The token your phone uses to push Health Connect data is now stored hashed. It is shown once when you create it and can be replaced at any time with Rotate. Each recorded sync can also be opened to see exactly which records it added and which it updated.

entries.title: Sun and outdoor time on Trends
entries.body: Trends → Vitals now charts daylight and outdoor time alongside your other vitals. A per-profile setting for which days are free of a fixed schedule sharpens the social jetlag reading for anyone whose week is not Monday to Friday.

entries.title: Allergies and gene results name the medications they affect
entries.body: An allergy row now lists the active medications it conflicts with, and a pharmacogenomic variant row lists the medications it affects — the same warnings, and the same dismissals, already shown on the medication side. Procedures and conditions also link back to the visit they came from.

entries.title: Report narratives now visible
entries.body: Narrative text read out of a report — ECG, stress test, imaging — is now shown on Results → Reports instead of being stored where nothing displayed it.

entries.title: Biomarkers for several people at once
entries.body: Results → Biomarkers can now show more than one household member together, each with their own section, reference ranges and starred markers.

operatorNotes: Health Connect ingest tokens can no longer be re-displayed after this upgrade. Use Rotate on the Health Connect page to mint a new one; phones already paired keep working with their existing token.
Database migrations 109–111 apply automatically on the first boot after upgrading.
